description: Convert a PDF bank or credit card statement on this computer with BankConv. Use this for a new PDF; for a statement converted earlier, use get_transactions or download_statement with its conversion id (list_conversions finds it). With output "transactions" (the default) it returns a summary and every transaction as JSON: ISO date, description, signed amount (money in positive), running balance; opening balances and totals are left out. Any other output saves that file and returns only its path and any warnings. csv: the statement as a spreadsheet; ofx: Xero, Sage, MYOB, QuickBooks Online; qfx: Quicken; qbo: QuickBooks Desktop (Web Connect); xero: Xero CSV with Xero's own columns. Uploading uses one BankConv page per PDF page. Waits until the conversion finishes. Errors say what went wrong: not_found for an unknown conversion id, gone once a conversion was deleted under data retention (24 hours by default), unreadable_statement when the tables can't be read as transactions (the message names the row), insufficient_credits when the account has too few pages.

file_path.description: Path to the PDF statement on this computer.

output.description: "transactions" returns the rows to you; any other value saves that file. csv: the statement as a spreadsheet; ofx: Xero, Sage, MYOB, QuickBooks Online; qfx: Quicken; qbo: QuickBooks Desktop (Web Connect); xero: Xero CSV with Xero's own columns.

password.description: The PDF password, if the statement is password-protected.

save_to.description: For file outputs: a file path or folder. Defaults to the PDF's folder, named after the PDF. An existing file at that path is overwritten.

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait for the conversion. On timeout the conversion keeps running; fetch it later with its conversion id.

name: convert_statement
title: Convert a bank statement PDF
